result.title: When Morphs Look Better: Face Image Quality as a Training-Free Signal for Morphing Attack Detection
result.summary: Face image quality assessment (FIQA) estimates the utility of a face image for automated face recognition and has been proposed as a morphing attack detection (MAD) signal that requires no morph-specific training. We evaluate 17 FIQA methods from all current FIQA categories on 20 morphing attack sets from two datasets, FRLL and FEI, including five diffusion-based attack sets. Each quality score is used directly as a MAD decision score. Unlike prior work, which inverted a quality measure when this lowered its error, we fix the score direction of each method in advance from its definition, so that cases in which morphs receive higher quality than bona fide samples remain visible. On FRLL, DifFIQA(R) achieves a mean D-EER of 11.42%, and together with CLIB-FIQA and eDifFIQA(L) clearly outperforms all other FIQA methods. A strong separation of bona fide and morph scores does not imply good detection performance: on the diffusion-based attacks, up to 11 of 17 methods assign higher quality to morphs than to bona fide samples, and the largest reversed separation in the study coincides with the worst detection result of the study. Performance also depends strongly on the attack: GraFIQs(L), the best detector of DCMorph and Arc2Morph on FRLL, performs poorly on the landmark-based and GAN-based attacks. On FEI, the lowest mean D-EER is 39.75%, and a threshold set on the bona fide data of one dataset does not transfer to the other.

AI.brief_summary: 在 FRLL 与 FEI 两个数据集的 20 个 morphed 攻击集上，评估 17 种人脸图像质量评估（FIQA）方法，并将其质量分数直接用作变形攻击检测的判决分数，且预先固定分数方向。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作属人脸生物特征取证与安全检测，关注质量分数方向、跨攻击与跨数据集的阈值迁移，未涉及 VLM 内部状态、视觉证据筛选或 latent 推理生成，缺少可供借鉴的具体线索。
